title: Best friend stole my Halloween costume
author: Storytime
hook: My best friend begged me to be a tree at her Halloween party. Now I know exactly why.
story: So every year I make my own Halloween costume. It's my thing. This year I spent six weeks on a moth queen costume with giant wings that actually open. I showed my best friend Mia every sketch. She loved them. She even asked for my exact measurements, for matching group shirts, she said. Then two weeks before the party she tells me she wants a group theme. An enchanted forest. And guess who gets to be the tree. Me. She said my wings would block everyone in the photos. Fine. I'm a team player. I show up in a brown bodysuit with twigs glued to my head. And Mia walks in wearing my moth queen. My wings. My colors. Even the little gold antennas I drew on page three. Turns out the party had a costume contest with a five hundred dollar prize. She entered it as her own design. She won. And in the winning photo I'm literally the tree standing behind her. Then the judge asked her to explain how the wings open. She couldn't. So she looked at me, and she said, tell them, you helped. And that's when I said something I probably shouldn't have. Part two if this gets enough comments.
caption: I was the tree. In MY OWN costume photo 🌳 #storytime
sound: a mysterious, slow Halloween piano at very low volume
why: Halloween week topic, a planted detail (the measurements) that pays off, a public humiliation everyone can picture, and a part two cliffhanger that drives follows.

title: Grandpa left me a key
author: Storytime
hook: My grandpa left my cousins his house. He left me one rusty key. Now they want to sue me.
story: My grandpa raised me for most of my teenage years. Every Sunday I helped him in his garage, fixing old engines nobody else cared about. My cousins only visited at Christmas, usually to ask for money. Grandpa used to joke that the best things he owned weren't in the house. I thought it was just a grandpa thing to say. When he passed, the lawyer read the will. The house went to my three cousins. The savings went to my aunt. And I got an envelope with one rusty key and an address two towns over. My cousins actually laughed. One of them said, enjoy your key. I drove to the address the next weekend. It was a storage unit. Inside, under dusty covers, were four classic cars. The same engines I'd helped him fix every Sunday. He had been restoring them for fifteen years, and he'd never told anyone. One of them is worth more than the house. There was a note on the dashboard in his handwriting. It said, you were the only one who showed up. Now my cousins say the cars should be split four ways, because they're family assets. My aunt agrees with them. So tell me honestly. Should I share?
caption: he always said the best things weren't in the house 🔑 #storytime
sound: an emotional, soft piano at very low volume
why: Inheritance plus underdog payoff is one of the most engaging storytime themes, the early line about the best things pays off in the twist, and the closing question drives comments from both sides.

title: Roommate labeled my name on a cake
author: Storytime
hook: I accused my roommate of stealing my food in our group chat. Then I opened the fridge.
story: So my roommate Tessa labels everything. Even her ketchup. For months my food kept disappearing. Yogurt. Pizza. A whole bag of cheese. Every time I asked, she said she had no idea. Last week I'd had enough. I posted in our apartment group chat that someone in this apartment is a thief, and we all know who labels everything except the food she steals. Everyone saw it. Tessa didn't reply. She just left the chat. That night I opened the fridge, and on the top shelf there was a cake box with a label. In Tessa's handwriting. It said my name. And under it, do not open until Friday. Friday is my birthday. I only mentioned it once, months ago. Inside was a homemade cake with my name on it. Next to it, a note from our other roommate, Jake. It said, sorry about your food, I'll pay you back. So Tessa never stole anything. She was planning my birthday the whole time. And I called her a thief in front of everyone. How do I even come back from this?
caption: I owe her the biggest apology of my life 🎂 #storytime
sound: a slow, slightly sad lo-fi beat at very low volume
why: Roommate food theft is instantly relatable, the label habit is set up early and becomes the twist, and asking viewers for advice pulls a lot of comments.
